title: 功率因数校正：并一个电容，电流变小了
summary: 电阻 + 电感的负载从信号发生器取电流，电流落后电压。按住按键并上一个 470 nF 电容：总电流变小、和电压对齐，电阻上的功率却不变。
concepts: 有功功率 P 与功率因数 cos θ active power, power factor
功率因数校正 power-factor correction
电流表有效值 RMS ammeter reading
取样电阻看电流 current-sense resistor
description: 信号发生器（正弦波 1.6 kHz、幅度 5 V）→ 电流表 AM1 → 结点 A → L1（10 mH）→ R1（100 Ω）→ S → RS（10 Ω）→ GND。按键 SW1 把 C1（470 nF）并在 A 和 S 之间。CH1 看 A，CH2 看 RS 上的电压（就是总电流的波形）。比较按下前后的总电流有效值和相位。

cards.title: 电流里有一部分在白跑
text: 信号发生器：**正弦波、`1.6 kHz`、幅度 `5 V`**。CH1 看负载上的电压，CH2 看 RS 上的电压——也就是总电流的形状。
电流（CH2）比电压晚到顶。负载里只有电阻会把电能变成热：信号发生器送来的电流，全都在干活吗？

cards.title: 电感借了能量又还回来
text: - 电感每四分之一周期把能量存进磁场，下一个四分之一周期又**原样还回去**。为了这一借一还，导线里要多跑一份电流，可它什么活也没干。
- 电容正好相反：电感在“借”的时候，电容在“还”。并上一个电容，这份来回跑的电流就在 L 和 C 之间**就地交换**，不用再从信号发生器那里绕一圈。
![](fig:pfc)
- 电阻真正用掉的功率是有功功率，它比“电压 × 电流”小，差的那个系数就是**功率因数**：
$$P = V I cos θ$$
例如电流落后 60° 时，$cos 60° = 0.5$：要输送同样的功率，导线里得跑两倍的电流。
- 并电容不改变电阻上的电压，所以不改变 P；它让 θ 变小，于是总电流 I 变小。
![](fig:phasors)

cards.title: 按下按键，比一比
text: - 正弦电流的**平均值**几乎是 0，所以在交流电路里，**电流表**的屏幕会自己换到 **AC RMS**（有效值）档：左上角写着 “AC RMS” 时，屏幕上的数就是要读的有效值。**点一下电流表**，右侧「属性」里还能看到平均值和有效值两行。
- **松开按键**：读电流表的有效值和 CH2 相对 CH1 的相位差。**点一下按键**让它保持按下：再读一次。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **功率因数** $cos θ$：有功功率和“电压 × 电流”之比。感性负载（电动机、变压器、日光灯镇流器）的电流落后电压，功率因数小于 1。
- **并联电容**补上电感要的那份来回的电流：有功功率不变，总电流变小，导线和发电机都轻松了。
- 坑：电容不是越大越好。补过头，电流反而**超前**电压，总电流又变大。工厂里的电容柜按负载分档投切，就是为了不补过头。
- 三相电和变压器的功率计算，都建立在同一个 $P = V I cos θ$ 上：去理论题里练。

caption.text: 负载是 R1 + L1；按住按键（S1 闭合），C1（彩色）就并在负载旁边。C1 的电流 I_C 和电感要的那份电流就地交换，信号发生器送来的总电流 I 变小。

i18n.en: The load is R1 + L1; hold the button (S1 closed) and C1 (in colour) sits beside it. C1's current I_C trades with the inductor's back-and-forth current on the spot, and the total current I from the generator gets smaller.

caption.text: 电流相量：负载电流 I_RL 落后电压；加上超前 90° 的 I_C，总电流 I 变短，而且几乎和电压同方向。

i18n.en: Current phasors: the load current I_RL lags the voltage; adding I_C, 90° ahead, makes the total I shorter and almost in line with the voltage.

en.title: Power-factor correction: add a capacitor, and the current drops
en.summary: A resistor + inductor load draws current from the generator, and the current lags the voltage. Hold a button to add a 470 nF capacitor in parallel: the total current gets smaller and lines up with the voltage, while the resistor's power stays the same.
concepts: active power P and power factor cos θ
en.description: Generator (sine 1.6 kHz, amplitude 5 V) → ammeter AM1 → node A → L1 (10 mH) → R1 (100 Ω) → S → RS (10 Ω) → GND. Button SW1 puts C1 (470 nF) between A and S. CH1 on A, CH2 across RS (the total current's waveform). Compare the total RMS current and the phase before and after pressing.

cards.title: Part of the current runs for nothing
text: The generator, the ammeter, the sense resistor **RS** (`10 Ω`) and both probes are already on the board. Add the load: **inductor** (`10 mH`) **`c6`**–**`c12`**, **resistor** (`100 Ω`) **`d12`**–**`d16`**.
Generator: **sine, `1.6 kHz`, amplitude `5 V`**. CH1 shows the voltage on the load, CH2 the voltage across RS — the shape of the total current.
The current (CH2) peaks after the voltage. Only the resistor turns electrical energy into heat: is all the current from the generator doing that work?

cards.title: The inductor borrows energy and gives it back
text: - Every quarter period the inductor stores energy in its magnetic field, and the next quarter it **gives it all back**. That borrowing and returning takes an extra share of current in the wires — current that does no work.

- A capacitor does the opposite: while the inductor borrows, the capacitor returns. Put a capacitor beside the load and that back-and-forth current is **traded on the spot** between L and C, instead of making the round trip through the generator.
![](fig:pfc)
- The power the resistor really uses is the active power. It is less than "voltage × current", and the factor between them is the **power factor**:
$$P = V I cos θ$$
For example, with the current 60° behind, $cos 60° = 0.5$: to deliver the same power the wires must carry twice the current.
- The capacitor does not change the voltage across the resistor, so P stays; it makes θ smaller, so the total current I drops.
![](fig:phasors)

cards.title: Press the button and compare
text: - **Push button** at **`e6`** (straddling the gap): pressed, it joins column `6` to column `8`. **Capacitor** (`470 nF`) into **`g8`**–**`g16`**, plus a short **jumper** **`e16`**–**`f16`** to join the two halves of column 16.

- The **average** of a sine current is almost 0, so in an AC circuit the **ammeter**'s screen switches itself to its **AC RMS** range: when the top left says "AC RMS", the number on the screen is the RMS value to read. **Click the ammeter** to see both the average and the RMS under Properties on the right.
- **Button released**: read the ammeter's RMS value and the phase of CH2 vs CH1. **Click the button** so it stays pressed, and read both again.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Power factor** $cos θ$: active power divided by "voltage × current". Inductive loads (motors, transformers, fluorescent-lamp ballasts) draw a lagging current, so their power factor is below 1.
- A **parallel capacitor** supplies the back-and-forth current the inductor needs: the active power stays, the total current drops, and the wires and the generator have an easier time.

- Pitfall: more capacitance is not better. Overcorrect and the current **leads** the voltage, and the total current grows again. Factory capacitor banks switch in steps with the load so they never overcorrect.
- Three-phase power and transformers rest on the same $P = V I cos θ$: practise them in the theory problems.

compare: - The load's impedance (with the coil's 1 Ω and the 10 Ω sense resistor): Z = 111 + j100.5 Ω, |Z| ≈ 150 Ω, so the current lags the voltage by about 42° (45° for R1 + L1 alone; RS makes the angle a little smaller). Power factor cos 42° ≈ 0.74.
- **Button released**: with the generator's internal 50 Ω the total RMS current is ≈ (5 V/√2) / |161 + j100.5| ≈ 18.6 mA.

- **Button pressed**: 470 nF at 1.6 kHz has a reactance of ≈ 212 Ω; its current leads by 90° and cancels the lagging part of the load current. The total current drops to ≈ 13.5 mA, with almost no phase difference (power factor ≈ 1).

- **R1's power**: the voltage at A hardly changes (less drop across the generator's 50 Ω, so it even rises a little), so R1's current rises by only about 2.6% (18.6 → 19.1 mA) and its power stays about the same — the active power is unchanged; only the back-and-forth current in the wires is gone.
- The capacitor for full correction: B_C = X_L/|Z_RL|² gives C ≈ 0.48 µF; 470 nF is the nearest standard value.

measurements.ask: Button released: the ammeter's RMS value (the screen shows AC RMS)
measurements.explain: Z = (100 + 1 + 10) + j100.5 Ω, plus the generator's internal 50 Ω: I = (5/√2) / |161 + j100.5| ≈ 18.6 mA.

measurements.ask: Button released: phase of CH2 (the current) vs CH1 (the load voltage)
measurements.explain: θ = arctan(100.5 / 111) ≈ 42°: the current lags, and the power factor cos θ ≈ 0.74.

measurements.ask: Button held: the ammeter's RMS value
measurements.explain: C1's current leads by 90° and cancels the lagging part of the load current; what remains of the total current is the part in phase with the voltage.

measurements.ask: Button held: phase of CH2 vs CH1
measurements.explain: Close to 0°: the power factor is close to 1. 470 nF is the standard value nearest to full correction (about 0.48 µF).

measurements.ask: After pressing the button, what happens to the power R1 uses (the active power)?
choices: About the same: the voltage across R1 hardly changed
More: the power factor went up
measurements.explain: The capacitor uses no energy and does not change the voltage across the load, so R1's power stays about the same (less drop across the generator's internal 50 Ω even lifts A a little). What dropped is the back-and-forth current in the wires.

hints: The load is one series branch: A (column 6) → inductor → resistor → S (column 16).
The button straddles the gap at e6: column 6 is one end, column 8 the other; the capacitor runs from the lower half of column 8 to the lower half of column 16.
Join the two halves of column 16 with a short jumper, so RS reaches both R1 and C1.
tests: Button released: the current lags the voltage
Button pressed: current and voltage almost in phase, smaller total current

tests.name: 松开按键：电流落后电压
按下按键：电流和电压几乎同相，总电流变小

compare: - 负载阻抗（含线圈电阻 1 Ω 和取样电阻 10 Ω）：Z = 111 + j100.5 Ω，|Z| ≈ 150 Ω，电流落后电压约 42°（只看 R1 + L1 是 45°，RS 让角度小了一点）。功率因数 cos 42° ≈ 0.74。
- **松开按键**：信号发生器内部还有 50 Ω，总电流有效值 ≈ (5 V/√2) / |161 + j100.5| ≈ 18.6 mA。
- **按下按键**：470 nF 在 1.6 kHz 的容抗 ≈ 212 Ω，它的电流超前 90°，正好抵掉负载电流里落后的那一部分。总电流降到 ≈ 13.5 mA，相位差接近 0（功率因数 ≈ 1）。
- **R1 的功率**：A 点电压几乎不变（信号发生器的 50 Ω 上压降变小，A 点电压反而略升），R1 的电流只多了约 2.6%（18.6 → 19.1 mA），功率基本不变——有功功率没变，只是导线里少跑了那份来回的电流。
- 完全补偿需要的电容：B_C = X_L/|Z_RL|² 时 C ≈ 0.48 µF；470 nF 是最接近的常用值。

measurements.ask: 松开按键：电流表的有效值（屏幕显示 AC RMS）
松开按键：CH2（电流）相对 CH1（负载电压）的相位差
measurements.explain: θ = arctan(100.5 / 111) ≈ 42°：电流落后，功率因数 cos θ ≈ 0.74。

measurements.ask: 按住按键：电流表的有效值
measurements.explain: C1 的电流超前 90°，抵掉了负载电流里落后的那一部分，总电流只剩和电压同相的那一份。

measurements.ask: 按住按键：CH2 相对 CH1 的相位差
measurements.explain: 接近 0°：功率因数接近 1。470 nF 是离完全补偿（约 0.48 µF）最近的常用值。

choices: 基本不变：R1 两端的电压几乎没变
变大了：功率因数变大了
measurements.ask: 按下按键后，R1 消耗的功率（有功功率）怎样？
measurements.explain: 电容不消耗能量，也没有改变负载两端的电压，所以 R1 的功率基本不变（信号发生器内部 50 Ω 上的压降变小，A 点电压还略升一点）。变小的是导线里来回跑的那份电流。

hints: 负载是一条串联支路：A（第 6 列）→ 电感 → 电阻 → S（第 16 列）。
按键横跨凹槽放在 e6：第 6 列是一端，第 8 列是另一端；电容从第 8 列下半接到第 16 列下半。
第 16 列上下两半要用一根短跳线接起来，RS 才同时接到 R1 和 C1。
